bull_thesis:
BULL CASE — SRPT at $16.8: a net-cash, cash-generative rare-disease franchise priced as a near-broken business, with a stabilizing commercial core and free, multi-shot pipeline optionality the market is valuing at roughly zero.

THE SETUP (why the price is the opportunity). The stock is $16.8 against a five-year revenue CAGR of +33.1% (FY2021 $702M → FY2025 $2.20B) and a balance sheet carrying Net debt −$614M (i.e., NET CASH). The market is pricing a permanent re-rating; the bull claim is that it has over-extrapolated a 2025 safety/execution shock into terminal decline of a franchise that is, in fact, stabilizing. The single most credible bullish signal in the entire file corroborates this: an INSIDER BUY RATIO OF 6.82 — insiders net buyers ~7:1 at these depressed prices — consistent with CFO Ian Estepan's Q1 2025 framing that the stock "is trading at levels that aren't even recognizing" the (then $2.3–2.6B) guidance and "we certainly think that it's undervalued." Management is voting with personal capital, not just rhetoric.

PILLAR 1 — THE CASH FLOOR IS REAL AND CONCRETE (this is the part of the story even the bear must concede). This is the one claim cluster the dossier grades as fully corroborated: "balance-sheet claims are true and corroborated (net cash, ~$750–950M liquidity, insiders buying)." Exited 2025 with "$954 million in cash and investments, growing $89 million in the fourth quarter" (Q4 2025); Q1 2026 cash $748M with "positive GAAP and non-GAAP earnings" and "positive cash flow, excluding Arrowhead-related payments." Critically, management PROACTIVELY removed the existential risk: it restructured to retire the 2027 convertible and explicitly prioritized "maintaining our revolver and addressing our 2027 convertible debt" (Q2 2025) — the dossier calls this "the single most important survival move." So the equity is not a liquidation/dilution candidate; Q1 2026: financial strength "allows us to fund our pipeline without relying on the equity markets." At a $16.8 price with ~$748M net cash and no near-term debt wall, downside is anchored by hard assets, not hope.

PILLAR 2 — A DURABLE, ANNUITY-LIKE PMO BASE THAT SURVIVED THE ENTIRE CRISIS UNTOUCHED. The dossier's verdict on the PMO franchise (EXONDYS/AMONDYS/VYONDYS) is the rare "MATCHES — the one durable claim." PMO revenue held in a tight ~$229–254M/qtr band across all eight quarters straight through two patient deaths, a black box, and a 36% RIF: $239M (Q2'24) → $249M (Q3'24) → $254M (Q4'24) → $237M (Q1'25) → $229M (Q1'26). This is ~$900M/yr of revenue underpinned by ">90%" weekly-infusion compliance "year after year after year" (Q4 2025) — a compliance rate that, as Estepan notes, patients "wouldn't be going through this level of burden if they weren't driving benefits" (Q2 2025). On top of stability, there is a genuine, under-priced CALL OPTION: in Q1 2026 Sarepta "submitted sNDAs seeking to transition [VYONDYS and AMONDYS] from accelerated approval to traditional approval" after the FDA "agreed that we could submit our clinical data and real-world evidence." Conversion to traditional approval would de-risk the most durable part of the business and remove the accelerated-approval-withdrawal tail risk entirely.

PILLAR 3 — THE COMMERCIAL BLEEDING HAS STOPPED, AND THE CLINICAL CASE IS STRENGTHENING (not weakening). The crux question the dossier poses is whether the ELEVIDYS collapse is "a timing/information problem (recoverable) or a permanent re-rating." Three pieces of evidence favor recoverable. (a) STABILIZATION IS, FOR ONCE, NOT CONTRADICTED BY THE SEQUENTIAL DATA — the dossier explicitly grants this green flag: "the Q1 2026 'stabilized' claim is, for once, not contradicted by the sequential ELEVIDYS trajectory flattening." Management guides Q1 2026 "about flat to perhaps down 15%" (Q4 2025) — i.e., the freefall from the $384M Q4'24 peak to $102M has flattened, not continued. (b) THE EFFICACY DATA DEEPENED THROUGHOUT THE CRISIS: three-year EMBARK data was "universally positive… the gap between ELEVIDYS-treated Duchenne boys and those who… have not yet been treated grows greater and greater with every passing year" (Q4 2025), reinforced in Q1 2026 by "supportive muscle MRI evidence showing that ELEVIDYS dystrophin helps protect muscle… less replacement by fat and fibrotic tissue." The clinical moat is widening even as the commercial number fell — a divergence that resolves bullishly if physicians re-engage. (c) THE ADDRESSABLE RUNWAY IS ENORMOUS AND BARELY PENETRATED: "Over 1,200 patients have already been treated… yet the majority of patients remain to be treated" (Q4 2025), rising to ">1,300" by Q1 2026; at Q4'24 management noted cumulative sales "represents less than 5% of the on-label addressable opportunity."

PILLAR 4 — A NON-AMBULATORY RE-OPENING CATALYST WITH A DATED READOUT AND A REAL-WORLD LEAD INDICATOR. The most lucrative segment (non-ambulatory) was removed from the label in 2025, so its return is pure upside not in any base case. The catalyst is concrete and dated: the FDA "approved our sirolimus pretreatment study for non-ambulatory patients… already enrolling… we expect results by the end of this year" (Q4 2025) — the ENDEAVOR Cohort 8 readout. The dossier flags the cleanest, least-spun signal in the entire file underpinning this bet: "More than 25% of sites are already using sirolimus on their own initiative" (Q1 2026) — a PHYSICIAN-LED, bottoms-up adoption signal management is legally barred from promoting ("we can't promote to it… comes entirely from physician practice"). Corroborating safety: in the interim real-world analysis "patients pretreated with sirolimus have shown no evidence of elevated liver enzyme to date" (Q1 2026). If Cohort 8 succeeds and re-opens the non-ambulatory label, the dossier's own framing is that "$16.8 against net cash of ~$748M, a stable ~$900M/yr PMO base, and free pipeline optionality is a deep-value setup that insiders are correctly buying at ~7:1."

PILLAR 5 — A FIVE-PROGRAM siRNA PIPELINE THE MARKET IS CAPITALIZING AT ~ZERO. The forward equity thesis now carries "five clinical stage programs" — DM1, FSHD, IPF, SCA2, and Huntington's — via the Arrowhead TRiM platform, with management claiming "potential to be best-in-class" addressing ">160,000 patients in the United States and multiples of that number internationally" (Q4 2025). Unlike the discredited financial guidance, the early biology has produced tangible, third-party-checkable signals: "positive preliminary data from our lead programs to treat FSHD and DM1" (Q1 2026), with the alpha-V-beta-6 integrin ligand showing "superior muscle concentration compared to transferrin-based approaches without dose-limiting toxicity" (Louise Rodino-Klapac, Q1 2026), and additional readouts explicitly scheduled for "the second half of this year." With the enterprise value compressed toward the cash floor, an investor is effectively paying ~nothing for five shots on goal in large rare-disease markets, each with a near-term catalyst.

MANAGEMENT QUALITY — DECISIVE AND, BELATEDLY, HONEST. The bull does not need to trust 2024 Doug Ingram; he needs 2026 Doug Ingram, who behaves differently. Rather than "stay the course… in the hope that things will self-correct" (which Ingram called the "irresponsible" path, Q2 2025), management cut ~$900M of cost and 36% of staff, killed the LGMD launch, and fixed the balance sheet — fast. Guidance discipline has been restored: management now tells investors to "model toward the low end of the range" (Q4 2025) and to exercise "prudence in raising estimates prematurely" (Q1 2026). The dossier credits this as a green flag: "Guidance discipline restored… management has learned from the over-promise and is now setting clearable bars." A low, conservatively-set bar that clears is a positive surprise engine.

PROBABILISTIC FRAME (how the bull wins). Base case (anchored, high-probability): ~$748M net cash + ~$900M/yr durable PMO annuity + ELEVIDYS stabilized at a ~$100M/qtr run-rate ≈ a sum-of-parts that is hard to reconcile with a $16.8 quote — i.e., the floor is already close to the price, limiting downside. The bull's expected value is then dominated by a stack of independent, dated call options, each free at this valuation: (1) VYONDYS/AMONDYS traditional-approval conversion (sNDAs filed, Q1 2026); (2) ENDEAVOR Cohort 8 sirolimus success re-opening the high-value non-ambulatory label (readout end-2026, with >25% physician-led adoption already as a tell); (3) an ELEVIDYS ambulatory re-acceleration in H2 2026 as the "information deficit" closes against deepening 3-year EMBARK/MRI evidence; (4) siRNA proof-of-concept reads (FSHD/DM1 H2 2026); (5) the long-tail DMD newborn-screening tailwind (added to the federal RUSP, Q4 2025). The conditions that must hold: cash burn stays inside the "cash flow positive… under all reasonable scenarios" promise (Q4 2025) so the optionality has time to mature; the PMO band does not break before traditional approval lands; and at least one of the four near-term catalysts converts. Given a price already near the demonstrable floor and insiders buying 7:1, the asymmetry is the thesis — you are paid to wait for options the market has written off.
bear_thesis:
BEAR CASE — SRPT: an early-stage biotech wearing a commercial-company costume, run by a team that missed its single biggest promise by ~30%+, where the only things you can underwrite are shrinking and the value case has migrated entirely onto unapproved assets.

THE CORE INDICTMENT (management's flagship promise was catastrophically wrong, in the same year). The bear case begins where management's credibility ended. The proud, repeated 2025 guidance of "$2.9 billion to $3.1 billion" (given verbatim Q2/Q3/Q4 2024) was cut mid-year to "$2.3 billion to $2.6 billion" (Q1 2025) and still missed, landing at ~$2.20B (FY2025 screener). The dossier's verdict: "MISS, badly… overshot reality by ~$0.8–0.9B. The original number was off by ~30%+." Worse, the "sustainable profitability" claim — "we became sustainably profitable and cash flow positive in 2024" → "the next globally relevant big biotech" (Q4 2024) — inverted inside ONE fiscal year: FY2024 NI +$235M / EPS +$2.34 collapsed to FY2025 NI −$713M / EPS −$7.13, with Net margin −32.5%, FCF margin −14.0%, ROE −67.5%, ROIC −14.2%. The dossier: "'sustainable' profitability lasted exactly one fiscal year." And the marquee long-range claim — "by the end of 2030, we will do over $16 billion cumulatively in operating income and over $13 billion in free cash flow" (Q4 2024) — was issued the very year the company swung to a $713M loss; the dossier rules it "UNSUPPORTED / fantastical… a discredited artifact." A bear underwrites this management's NUMBERS at a steep discount because the historical record says their forecasts are unreliable precisely when it matters.

THE BUSINESS YOU CAN ACTUALLY UNDERWRITE IS SHRINKING ~45% AND THE FLAGSHIP HAS LOST 70%+. Strip the optionality and look at the contractual reality. ELEVIDYS quarterly revenue ran $122M → $181M → $384M (peak Q4'24) → $375M → and then COLLAPSED to $102M by Q1 2026 — a >70% peak-to-trough fall in the supposed crown jewel. The dossier: "the emphatic 'no bottleneck' framing preceded a >70% peak-to-trough collapse." Total net product revenue is now guided to "$1.2 billion to $1.4 billion" for 2026 (Q4 2025), with management itself steering to the floor: "without our educational efforts, we would expect to track to $1.2 billion… model toward the low end." That codifies a FURTHER ~45% revenue contraction off FY2025's $2.20B. Q1 2026 already printed total revenue of just $331M ($229M PMO + $102M ELEVIDYS), an annualized run-rate consistent with the low end. The thing the market can measure is going DOWN, hard; everything pointing up is an unapproved promise.

"RETURN TO GROWTH" IS A SEMANTIC TRAP — IT MEANS AMBULATORY-ONLY, AND THE PROFITABLE SEGMENT IS GONE. The bull leans on "the business is stabilized" and "positioned to return to growth" (Q1 2026). But on direct cross-examination the claim shrank: asked whether return-to-growth assumes non-ambulatory resumption, Ingram conceded "we're talking about in the ambulatory population RIGHT NOW… non-ambulatory is not in our label" (Q1 2026). The most lucrative segment — non-ambulatory, the entire reason the June-2024 broad label was celebrated as covering "over 80% of patients" — was REMOVED from the label after two deaths and "non-ambulatory dosing is halted" (Q2 2025), and remains out. So "growth" is off a depressed ambulatory-only base, and the high-value population is contingent on a single unread study (below). The dossier's framing of the downside: if the hesitation is "rational physician response to a changed safety profile — not a fixable information gap — then the 2026 guide is a CEILING, not a floor."

THE "INFORMATION DEFICIT" IS A MANUFACTURED EUPHEMISM FOR A SAFETY-AND-DEMAND PROBLEM. Management reframes the commercial shortfall as an "information deficit" causing "patient and physician hesitation" (Q4 2025) — i.e., a communication problem that "well-designed plans" and "educational efforts" can fix. The dossier is blunt: this is "a carefully engineered euphemism… It reframes a demand and safety problem (two deaths, a black box, families pausing) as a communication problem… locating the failure outside the product… management's most sensitive pressure point, semantically disguised." The bear's null hypothesis: physicians are not under-informed — they are CORRECTLY informed about a gene therapy that now carries a black box warning and two acute-liver-failure deaths, and are rationally pausing. If that is true, re-education does not bend the curve, the H2-2026 "inflection" management keeps deferring never arrives, and the $1.4B high end of guidance is unreachable.

THE SAFETY NARRATIVE IS NOT CLOSED — A FRESH FATALITY SURFACED IN Q1 2026. This is not purely historical. In Q1 2026, H.C. Wainwright's analyst surfaced a NEW FDAERS "fatality due to cardiac breathing issues… reported 3 weeks ago"; management deemed it "unrelated… nearly 14 months post treatment" (Louise Rodino-Klapac, Q1 2026) — plausibly true, but it demonstrates the adverse-event tail is live and the headline risk recurring. Compounding the concern: when pressed in Q2 2025 on "how many patients have had ALF cases" and hospitalization trends, Ingram could not or would not quantify the safety denominator — "I don't have that… if you're dehydrated, you get hospitalized." For a gene therapy with two deaths and a black box, an inability to state the safety denominator is, in the dossier's words, "a genuine red flag." Any third ELEVIDYS-attributed event would be thesis-ending.

THE DURABLE PMO BASE IS NOT AS SAFE AS IT LOOKS — ESSENCE MISSED, AND COMPETITION ARRIVED. The bull's annuity has two fresh cracks. First, the ESSENCE confirmatory trial "did not reach statistical significance on the primary endpoint, the 4-step Ascend" (Q3 2025); management retreated to exactly the pre-positioned rescue vocabulary analysts flagged a year earlier — "COVID appears to have had an impact," "when one excludes the COVID participants… benefit… by about 30%," and a "prognostic score" subgroup with "p-value of 0.01." The dossier's "totality of evidence" tell: that phrase "is a reliable marker that a clean statistical result was NOT achieved and a narrative is being constructed around the data instead of from it." The sNDAs for traditional approval (filed Q1 2026) now rest on post-hoc subgroups and real-world evidence against a MISSED primary endpoint — far from a sure conversion, and a failure to convert leaves the accelerated approvals exposed. Second, the moat is visibly eroding: Ingram moved from "there is no one near us today" (Q3 2024) to conceding a real EXONDYS competitor — "I think it will be real competition" (Dye, Q4 2025). The one "durable" pillar faces a confirmatory-trial overhang AND new competition simultaneously.

THE EQUITY THESIS HAS MIGRATED ONTO ASSETS WITH ZERO APPROVALS AND ZERO REVENUE. Tellingly, by Q1 2026 the value case rests on the siRNA pipeline — DM1, FSHD, IPF, SCA2, Huntington's — described as "potentially best-in-class" (Q4 2025/Q1 2026). But these are early reads: "positive PRELIMINARY data" (Q1 2026), with pivotal results perpetually "in the second half of this year." The dossier red-flags this directly: "Forward equity thesis now rests on unapproved siRNA assets… 'encouraging early signals' but ZERO approvals and ZERO revenue; the base business is shrinking while the story migrates to optionality." That is the structural problem: the bull is asked to pay a commercial-company narrative for what is, in cash-flow terms, an early-stage biotech whose revenue line is contracting ~45% and whose value increasingly depends on Phase I/II biology.

PATTERN EVIDENCE — MANAGEMENT WAS CONFIDENTLY WRONG ABOUT EVERY RISK THAT LATER MATERIALIZED, AND BROKE AN EXPLICIT PROMISE. The dossier's analyst-pressure section is a catalog of dismissed-then-realized risks: capacity ("we don't have bottlenecks. We have a launch curve," Q2 2024 → three quarters later "60% of our current revenue comes from top sites… booked out to 12 months," Q1 2025); payer friction (channel-check denials "brushed aside"); the ESSENCE binary (deflected with "totality of evidence" a full year before the miss). Most damning, a concrete, falsifiable commitment failed: "I don't intend to do it again" on guidance cuts (Q1 2025) — broken within two quarters when the framework was abandoned entirely (Q2 2025). The C-suite exit of Chief Customer Officer Dallan Murray — the executive who delivered the most confident "we know exactly who's lined up… very, very granular detail" forecast — "coincides exactly with the commercial forecast's collapse" (dossier). When the person who made the forecast leaves as the forecast implodes, a bear treats the remaining forecasts as suspect.

WHAT WOULD CONFIRM THE BEAR (and the probabilistic frame). The bear wins if: (1) ELEVIDYS shows NO quantified start-form/revenue inflection in H2 2026 — management has repeatedly promised data "at a later time" (Patrick Moss, Q3 2025) and as of Q1 2026 the recovery "remained prospective"; the absence of a hard inflection confirms the hesitation is structural, not informational. (2) ENDEAVOR Cohort 8 sirolimus FAILS or is delayed, foreclosing the non-ambulatory re-opening and leaving the franchise capped at an ambulatory-only, ~$1.2B-and-falling base. (3) The VYONDYS/AMONDYS sNDAs do NOT convert to traditional approval, given they lean on a missed primary endpoint and post-hoc subgroups. (4) Any new ELEVIDYS-attributed safety event. (5) Cash continues to bleed — note the draw from $954M (Q4'25) to $748M (Q1'26), a ~$206M sequential decline including Arrowhead payments; sustained burn while revenue falls would force the very equity-market reliance management says it can avoid, re-introducing dilution risk. The probabilistic verdict: the dossier scores CREDIBILITY 2/10 and TRAJECTORY "PIVOTING (forced)." A bear sizes to the reality that you are underwriting a shrinking ~$1.2B-revenue, loss-making business (FY2025 −$713M) whose recovery depends on a stack of binary, unproven catalysts run by a team that "already missed its biggest promise once" — and "the burden of proof sits squarely" with them. Net cash is a floor under a melting ice cube, not a reason to own the equity ahead of the proof.
consensus_delta:
FRAMED THROUGH THE INNOVATION/CATALYST LENS, REGIME-ADJUSTED for 2026-06-05 (late-cycle melt-up on an unresolved oil/inflation shock, WTI ~$92, CPI 3.8%, Fed higher-for-longer to ~Dec, BofA FMS cash 3.9%, AI-capex ~40% of 2026 EPS growth, an M&A/regulatory window that may NARROW after the Nov-2026 midterms). This is a HYBRID — an innovation-classified name trading at a deep-value price ($16.8, net debt −$614M, MOS effectively floored by the balance sheet) — so the expectations-arbitrage question has two halves, and the regime SHARPENS rather than softens the asymmetry.

HALF ONE — WHERE THE STREET IS TOO BEARISH (the real, but bounded, edge), and how the regime AMPLIFIES the floor's value. The market prices SRPT as a near-broken business: at $16.8 the enterprise value compresses toward the ~$748M cash floor, assigning roughly ZERO to (i) a durable ~$900M/yr PMO annuity that held a tight $229–254M/qtr band through two deaths, a black box, a 36% RIF, and the ELEVIDYS collapse (dossier: 'MATCHES — the one durable claim'), and (ii) five clinical-stage siRNA programs with near-term reads. The factually-incorrect consensus assumption is that the ELEVIDYS revenue line is in TERMINAL decline; the sequential tape says the freefall from $384M (Q4'24) to $102M (Q1'26) has FLATTENED, and the dossier grants the one green flag that matters here: 'the Q1 2026 stabilized claim is, for once, NOT contradicted by the sequential ELEVIDYS trajectory.' Insiders buying ~7:1 (ratio 6.82) into the tape is the corroborating arb signal. REGIME OVERLAY (point d — resolution-driver INDEPENDENCE): the single most valuable regime property of this name is that its resolution drivers — ELEVIDYS re-education, Cohort 8 sirolimus, sNDA conversion, siRNA biology — are IDIOSYNCRATIC and ORTHOGONAL to the macro factor that dominates the tape (oil, CPI, AI-capex, the Fed path). In a melt-up where ~30% of the index is Mag-7 and ~40% of 2026 EPS growth is AI-capex, an uncorrelated, net-cash, clinical-binary special-sit is a genuinely diversifying source of return — and its hard-asset floor is itself macro-insensitive: a CPI print or an oil spike does not impair $748M of cash. That is a real, regime-relevant reason the street's terminal-decline pricing is too harsh.

HALF TWO — WHERE THE STREET (AND THE BULL) IS TOO OPTIMISTIC, and why the regime makes the edge MORE bounded, not less. The dossier scores CREDIBILITY 2/10 for cause: every QUANTIFIED forecast this management made was wrong precisely when it mattered ($2.9–3.1B → cut to $2.3–2.6B → missed at $2.20B; 'sustainable profitability' reversed inside one fiscal year into −$713M; the $16B-by-2030 figure issued on the eve of that loss). So the arbitrage CANNOT be underwritten on management's numbers — only on the cash floor + PMO base as 'known,' with ELEVIDYS recovery and siRNA as OPTIONS. The street assumption I will NOT bet against is the 2026 revenue contraction: management steered to '$1.2B… model toward the low end,' codifying a further ~45% decline off $2.20B, and Q1 2026's $331M total run-rate confirms it. REGIME OVERLAY (point c + valley): in a higher-for-longer regime the option half of this thesis is the most rate-sensitive part of the capital structure — Phase I/II siRNA value and a deferred ELEVIDYS re-acceleration are long-duration cash flows whose present value is mechanically compressed by a stuck-higher discount rate; a Fed on hold to ~Dec offers NO multiple-relief tailwind to the optionality. And the regime explicitly DEPRIORITIZES hard-binary/clinical-regulatory catalysts as the thinnest-edge lane — which is exactly the lane SRPT's upside lives in. NET CONSENSUS DELTA (regime-adjusted): the street is too bearish on the FLOOR (net cash + PMO + free optionality is worth more than ~zero, and that floor is macro-proof) but correctly bearish on the NEAR-TERM TRAJECTORY (revenue is contracting, the recovery is unproven, and the regime gives the unproven half no discount-rate help). That asymmetry — macro-insensitive downside protection plus uncorrelated but un-dated, rate-pressured upside, against a credibility-impaired, still-shrinking, binary-catalyst core — is a WATCHLIST setup, not an aggressive-entry mispricing. The good news is real but NOT in the tape on a hard, in-window date — the precise condition for B over A under this regime.
forcing_function:
This is the decisive section, and under the 2026-06-05 regime it is what most firmly pins the verdict to B rather than A — because the regime's explicit FORCING-FUNCTION test (reward a hard-dated catalyst INSIDE the H1/mid-2026 window; PENALIZE a thesis whose catalyst is out-of-window) is one SRPT FAILS on timing, even though it PASSES on not needing a rate rescue. As of the 2026-06-05 evaluation date (with the Q1 2026 call, 2026-05-06, already digested), the catalyst calendar is:

THE DECISIVE FORCING FUNCTION — ENDEAVOR COHORT 8 SIROLIMUS READOUT, expected 'by the end of this year' (END-2026, per Q4 2025). This is THE event that shatters consensus in either direction: SUCCESS re-opens the high-value NON-AMBULATORY label removed in 2025 (the segment that justified the original 'over 80% of patients' valuation) and validates the deep-value sum-of-parts, with >25% physician-led sirolimus adoption and 'no evidence of elevated liver enzyme to date' (Q1 2026) as real-world lead indicators; FAILURE/DELAY forecloses the comeback and caps the franchise at an ambulatory-only, ~$1.2B-and-falling base. BUT under the regime mandate this catalyst is PENALIZED on two counts: (a) it sits OUT-OF-WINDOW — end-2026 is past the H1/mid-2026 window the regime rewards, and it also lands AFTER the Nov-2026 midterms, beyond the open M&A/regulatory window that the regime warns may NARROW; (b) it is a HARD-BINARY clinical/regulatory event — exactly the PDUFA-type lane the regime singles out as the THINNEST edge and instructs me to DEPRIORITIZE in favor of structural distressed/deleveraging special-sits. SRPT is NOT a clean distressed/deleveraging or forced-seller setup; it is a binary-catalyst biotech, which is the regime's least-favored archetype. That is a direct, mandated drag on conviction.

SECONDARY FORCING FUNCTIONS (the tells that front-run the big one), with regime timing applied: (1) A QUANTIFIED ELEVIDYS START-FORM / REVENUE INFLECTION in the H2 2026 prints (Q2/Q3 2026 calls) — the dossier's explicit gating evidence ('demand two pieces of hard evidence before adding'). This is the EARLIEST hard tell, but note it is H2-weighted and still back-of-mid-2026; a numeric start-form pickup converts the 'information deficit' thesis from spin to fact, while its ABSENCE confirms the bear. (2) VYONDYS/AMONDYS sNDA traditional-approval decisions (filed Q1 2026) — conversion de-risks the durable PMO pillar; a negative signal (given the missed ESSENCE primary) cracks the one 'known' asset. (3) siRNA FSHD/DM1 proof-of-concept reads scheduled for 'the second half of this year' — free options on a pipeline valued at ~zero, but again back-half and rate-pressured. CRITICAL REGIME GAP: there is NO hard-dated UPSIDE forcing function INSIDE the H1/mid-2026 window. Every catalyst that could re-rate the equity is back-half-or-end-2026 and binary — the regime rewards in-window hard dates and SRPT has none. NET: the EXACT EVENT TO WAIT FOR (the regime-aware B trigger): EITHER (i) a quantified ELEVIDYS start-form/revenue inflection in the next 1–2 prints (the first H2-2026 tell), OR (ii) positive de-risking into/at the Cohort 8 readout (end-2026), OR (iii) a regime-driven beta flush (see positioning) that resets the entry low enough that the out-of-window, binary catalyst stack no longer needs to be paid for. Enter ON that de-risking or that flush, sizing to the cash floor + PMO annuity as base. The regime supplies NO near-dated upside forcing function to justify an A today — and it actively penalizes the out-of-window, hard-binary nature of the catalysts that do exist.
valley_of_death:
INNOVATION-LENS read, REGIME-ADJUSTED, and this is the section the 2026-06-05 macro most directly worsens. Start with what the regime does NOT threaten: there is NO solvency valley. Net cash −$614M, the 2027 convertible proactively retired (dossier: 'the single most important survival move'), and 'financial strength… allows us to fund our pipeline without relying on the equity markets' (Q1 2026). Critically — and this is a regime POSITIVE — SRPT does NOT need a Fed cut, a rate rescue, or any easing of financial conditions to survive; the higher-for-longer path that punishes leveraged, refinancing-dependent issuers does not bear on a net-cash balance sheet with no near-term maturity wall. The enterprise will not be forced into a dilutive raise or a covenant breach in the next 3–9 months. The risk is to the STOCK and the THESIS CLOCK, not to survival.

WHAT WILL PRESSURE THE STOCK / THESIS INSIDE 3–9 MONTHS (i.e., before the decisive end-2026 catalyst), with the regime tails layered on: (1) THE REVENUE TROUGH IS STILL AHEAD IN THE PRINTS. 2026 is guided to $1.2–1.4B vs FY2025 $2.20B (a further ~45% contraction), management itself steering to the floor. The Q2/Q3 2026 prints will show YoY revenue DOWN sharply and likely continued GAAP losses (FY2025 −$713M / EPS −$7.13). In a stretched, fully-invested melt-up with FMS cash at 3.9% and little dry powder to absorb disappointments, a loss-making name printing in-line-but-still-shrinking quarters is exactly the profile that gets sold first in any risk-off air-pocket — the regime RAISES the beta of each soft print. (2) THE ELEVIDYS INFLECTION IS PROSPECTIVE, NOT PROVEN. The dossier is explicit that as of Q1 2026 the recovery 'remained prospective' and start-form data keeps being deferred 'to a later time' (Patrick Moss, Q3 2025). interrogator_dossier:
# Forensic Dossier — Sarepta Therapeutics (SRPT)

*Coverage: 8 consecutive earnings calls, Q2 2024 (2024-08-07) through Q1 2026 (2026-05-06). Management transcripts cross-referenced against screener financials (multi-year trajectory FY2021–FY2025, latest fiscal year FY2025). Current price $16.8 against a five-year revenue CAGR of +33% — the market is pricing this as a near-broken business, and the transcripts explain why.*

---

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

Few companies in this coverage universe travel further from triumph to crisis inside eight quarters than Sarepta does. The arc is not a drift — it is a fall, with a precise inflection point, and management's language tracks it almost in real time.

**Chapter 1 — "Project Moonshot achieved" / coronation (Q2 2024 – Q4 2024).** The story opens at the apex. In June 2024 Sarepta won a **broad ELEVIDYS label** covering "over 80% of patients living with and dying from Duchenne muscular dystrophy" (Q2 2024), the event CEO Doug Ingram says he joined the company seven years earlier to deliver. The framing is maximal and self-congratulatory: "we are second to no one in the world at launching Duchenne therapies" (Q2 2024); ELEVIDYS is "the largest gene therapy yet approved." Management hands out **explicit, large, multi-quarter guidance**: 2025 net product revenue of **"$2.9 billion to $3.1 billion"** across four therapies, "two-thirds of which will come from ELEVIDYS," repeated verbatim in Q2, Q3, and Q4 2024. By Q4 2024 the rhetoric peaks with **"Project Moonshot,"** a claim to have "achieved all of the goals" and a stunning long-range promise: "by the end of 2030, we will do over $16 billion cumulatively in operating income and over $13 billion in free cash flow." The growth surface is simultaneously *expanded* via the **Arrowhead siRNA collaboration** (closed Feb 2025), adding "multiple potential blockbuster siRNA launches before the end of this decade," and a **three-launch LGMD franchise** (SRP-9003/9004/9005) promised across "the next three years."

**Chapter 2 — first crack (Q1 2025).** The tone breaks. Ingram opens by conceding Sarepta "faced challenges that have motivated us to take a more measured view." The headline is the **first ELEVIDYS death** — "a boy infused with ELEVIDYS suffered an acute liver failure and passed away" — and the **first guidance cut in his career**: 2025 revenue lowered from $2.9–3.1B to **"$2.3 billion to $2.6 billion."** Three causes are offered: the safety event ("families... to pause"), administrative cycle times "one month to six weeks longer than our original estimates," and a top-site capacity imbalance ("60% of our current revenue comes from top sites... booked out to 12 months"). Tellingly, Ingram pre-commits: "it's the first time frankly, in my career when I've done it, and I don't intend to do it again" (Q1 2025). He would break that promise within two quarters.

**Chapter 3 — restructuring / survival (Q2 2025, special call July 18).** This is not a normal earnings call; it is a **strategic-restructure call**, and the language is existential. A **second ALF death** has occurred. The FDA imposes a **black box warning** on the ambulatory label and **non-ambulatory dosing is halted**. Management announces: a **36% reduction in force (~500 employees)**, **~$900M of cost cuts through 2027**, the **shelving of the entire LGMD launch franchise** (9003 partially retained, 9004/9005 "paused" for partners), explicit prioritization of **retiring the 2027 convertible note**, and a **C-suite reshuffle** in which long-tenured Chief Customer Officer **Dallan Murray departs**. The thesis has inverted from "next globally relevant big biotech" (Q4 2024) to "remain profitable, cash flow positive and capable of addressing our financial obligations" (Q2 2025). Ingram even cancels the August earnings call to save cost.

**Chapter 4 — confirmatory miss (Q3 2025).** The PMO franchise — the supposed durable base — takes a hit: the **ESSENCE confirmatory trial misses its primary endpoint** (4-step Ascend, p not significant). Management pivots hard to post-hoc rescue: "COVID appears to have had an impact," and "when one excludes the COVID participants, we see a meaningful treatment benefit... by about 30%." The defensive vocabulary ("totality of the evidence," "real-world evidence," subgroup "prognostic score") dominates.

**Chapter 5 — "strong footing" reset (Q4 2025, 2026-02-25 — the conviction-input quarter).** Management attempts to draw a line under the crisis: "we've entered 2026 on a strong footing... three pillars." But the numbers expose the magnitude of the fall. Having abandoned guidance entirely, they reintroduce **2026 net product revenue guidance of just $1.2–1.4B** — roughly **60% below the original $3B 2025 vision** — and concede Q1 2026 will be "about flat to perhaps down 15%." The commercial shortfall is rebranded as an **"information deficit"** causing "patient and physician hesitation." Cash is the headline comfort: "$954 million in cash and investments."

**Chapter 6 — "stabilized" (Q1 2026).** ELEVIDYS quarterly revenue has collapsed to **$102M** (from a $384M peak in Q4 2024). Management asserts "the business has stabilized" and "is positioned to return to growth" — but on cross-examination concedes that "return to growth" means **the ambulatory population only**; non-ambulatory remains out of the label. Cash has drawn down to **$748M**. The forward story has fully migrated to the **siRNA pipeline** (DM1, FSHD, Huntington's, IPF, SCA2) — "potentially best-in-class" — i.e., the value case now rests on assets with *no approvals and no revenue.*

**Net arc:** A company that opened by promising $3B in 2025 and $16B cumulative operating income by 2030 ends by guiding to $1.2B, having cut a third of its staff, killed its second growth franchise, taken two patient deaths and a black box warning, missed its confirmatory trial, and repositioned the entire equity thesis onto an unapproved siRNA pipeline. Growth drivers **introduced**: Arrowhead siRNA (Q4 2024). Drivers **dropped or gutted**: LGMD launch franchise (shelved Q2 2025), ELEVIDYS non-ambulatory population (halted Q2 2025), the entire $2.9–3.1B/$16B Moonshot guidance architecture (abandoned 2025).

---

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

This is where the dossier earns its keep. Management's biggest *quantified* claims were made in 2024 and then systematically failed against 2025 reality. The screener's multi-year line — **FY2024 NI +$235M / EPS +$2.34, collapsing to FY2025 NI −$713M / EPS −$7.13** — is the single most damning piece of evidence, and it directly contradicts the "sustainably profitable, cash flow positive" refrain.

| Management claim (quarter) | Financial evidence (screener) | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| 2025 net product revenue "**$2.9 billion to $3.1 billion**" (Q2/Q3/Q4 2024, repeated as high-conviction) | FY2025 revenue landed at **$2.20B**; the year was *cut to $2.3–2.6B (Q1 '25)* then missed even that trajectory | **MISS, badly.** The flagship guidance overshot reality by ~$0.8–0.9B. The original number was off by ~30%+. |
| "We **became sustainably profitable and cash flow positive** in 2024" → "next globally relevant big biotech" (Q4 2024) | FY2024 NI +$235M (the *one* profitable year), then **FY2025 NI −$713M, EPS −$7.13**; FY2025 **Net margin −32.5%, FCF margin −14.0%** | **DIVERGES sharply.** "Sustainable" profitability lasted exactly one fiscal year before reversing to the largest loss in the five-year window. |
| "By the end of 2030... **over $16 billion cumulatively in operating income and over $13 billion in free cash flow**" (Q4 2024) | FY2025 swung to a $713M loss and *negative* FCF; ROE −67.5%, ROIC −14.2% | **UNSUPPORTED / fantastical.** A claim made the same year the business turned deeply loss-making. The director should treat the $16B figure as a discredited artifact. |
| ELEVIDYS demand "robust," "no bottlenecks... we have a launch curve" (Q2 2024); "we don't have a bottleneck that we need to solve for" | ELEVIDYS revenue ran $122M → $181M → $384M (peak Q4'24) → $375M → then **collapsed to $102M by Q1 2026** | **CONTRADICTED.** The emphatic "no bottleneck" framing preceded a >70% peak-to-trough collapse in the flagship product. |
| "Margin... trending towards 90%" with suspension manufacturing, margins "improve in the 2027 timeframe" (Q4 2024) | FY2025 **Gross margin 59.9% and flagged *contracting***; net cash but ROIC −14.2% | **DIVERGES.** Gross margin is going the wrong way relative to the 90% aspiration; the improvement is pushed to 2027 (always two years out). |
| PMOs are a "**healthy and solid**," "durable" base; "compliance rate... over 90%" (Q2 2024 → Q4 2025) | PMO revenue genuinely stable (~$229–254M/qtr across the window) | **MATCHES — the one durable claim.** PMOs held ~flat even through the crisis; this is the most credible part of the story. *But* ESSENCE then missed (see §5), threatening the *traditional-approval* upside, not the current base. |
| "We are well positioned to weather this chaotic period... strong P&L and balance sheet" (Q1 2025) | **Net debt −$614M (i.e., net cash)**; cash $954M (Q4'25) → $748M (Q1'26) | **MATCHES on the balance sheet; MISLEADS on the P&L.** Liquidity is real and is the genuine floor. But pairing "strong P&L" with a −$713M FY2025 net result is rhetorical sleight of hand. |
| 2026 guidance "$1.2 billion to $1.4 billion... track to $1.2 billion... model toward the low end" (Q4 2025) | Implies a *further* decline from FY2025's $2.20B | **HONEST, finally.** This is the first guidance that appears conservatively set rather than aspirational — but it codifies a ~45% revenue contraction off FY2025. |
| Buyback consideration — stock "undervalued," "trading at levels that aren't even recognizing" guidance (Q1 2025, Ian Estepan) | Price **$16.8**; **insider buy ratio 6.82** (insiders heavily net buyers) | **PARTIALLY CORROBORATED by insider behavior.** Insiders are buying ~7:1 — a genuine signal of management conviction at depressed prices — but no aggressive buyback was actually disclosed, and the stock kept falling. Conviction ≠ vindication. |

**Net:** The *balance-sheet* claims are true and corroborated (net cash, ~$750–950M liquidity, insiders buying). The *growth, profitability, and long-range value* claims are richer-than-the-numbers to the point of being discredited — the $3B guidance missed, "sustainable profitability" reversed inside a year into a $713M loss, and the $16B-by-2030 promise was made on the eve of the collapse. The story management told in 2024 and the trajectory the company actually delivered in 2025 are not the same story. A director must underwrite **only the cash floor and the PMO base as "known"**, and treat everything ELEVIDYS-recovery and siRNA as *option value, not base case.*

---

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Trajectory: DECLINING (sharply, Q4 2024 → Q2 2025), then a deliberate, defensive re-stabilization (Q3 2025 → Q1 2026).**

| Quarter | Tone | Quoted evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Q2 2024 | **Euphoric / offensive** | "we are second to no one in the world at launching Duchenne therapies"; "we don't have a bottleneck... we have a launch curve." |
| Q3 2024 | **Confident / offensive** | "another strong quarter"; "ELEVIDYS performance substantially exceeded our prior guidance"; "the launch is going swimmingly." |
| Q4 2024 | **Peak triumphalism** | "Project Moonshot... we achieved all of the goals"; "the next globally relevant big biotech"; "$16 billion cumulatively in operating income" by 2030. |
| Q1 2025 | **First defensive break** | "a more measured view"; "we... fell short of expectations"; "it's not enjoyable to bring guidance down. It's the first time frankly, in my career." Emotional close referencing attending "a funeral yesterday for a young man who died of Duchenne." |
| Q2 2025 | **Crisis / damage-control** | "various challenging unexpected and impactful events"; "complacency would be irresponsible"; "reduction in force... about 36% of our workforce"; "This risk is personally very painful to me." |
| Q3 2025 | **Defensive / explanatory** | "the study did not reach statistical significance on the primary endpoint"; "COVID appears to have had an impact"; "we believe we have a good argument for traditional approval." |
| Q4 2025 | **Reassurance / reset** | "we've entered 2026 on a strong footing"; "three pillars to our strength"; reframes shortfall as an "information deficit" and "physician hesitation." |
| Q1 2026 | **Cautious optimism / hedged** | "the business is stabilized"; "positioned to return to growth" — but immediately qualified to "the ambulatory population right now" and "would counsel prudence in raising estimates prematurely." |

**Language shift from offensive to defensive is unambiguous.** Through 2024 the vocabulary is growth, demand, launch, leadership, blockbuster, Moonshot. From Q1 2025 it migrates to cost, restructuring, obligations, convertible debt, floor, stress test, prudence, totality of evidence. By Q2 2025 Ingram is explicitly defending the *viability* of the firm, not its ambition. The "stabilized" tone of Q1 2026 is real but defensive — it is the language of a company arguing it has stopped the bleeding, not one describing growth.

**Specificity of guidance over time — a critical tell.** Management was *maximally* specific when it was wrong (precise $2.9–3.1B and $16B figures in 2024) and went *guidance-free* exactly when investors needed numbers most (declined to guide 2026 until forced, Q4 2025). When they finally re-guide, they pre-apologize and steer to the low end. This is the opposite of a sandbagging pattern — it is a credibility-repair pattern after over-promising.

---

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

**Reliability: LOW** (on revenue/financial guidance), with a partial offset for honesty *after* the fall.

The forensic record on guidance-vs-delivery is poor:

- **2025 revenue guidance ($2.9–3.1B, given Q2–Q4 2024) → cut to $2.3–2.6B (Q1 2025) → actual FY2025 ~$2.20B.** A two-step miss; the original flagship number overshot by ~30–40%. This is the central credibility failure of the entire coverage window.
- **"I don't intend to [cut guidance] again" (Q1 2025) → guidance abandoned entirely by mid-2025, then re-set ~60% lower for 2026 (Q4 2025).** The explicit promise not to cut again was broken within two quarters (the restructure call effectively withdrew the framework).
- **Q4 2024 ELEVIDYS "exceeded guidance by $60M / full year by $100M"** — *true* for that quarter, and it is the reason management earned the benefit of the doubt going into 2025. The beat history is genuinely mixed: the screener shows **beat 4/7 quarters (57%)**, i.e., barely above a coin flip, and the misses clustered exactly when it mattered (the 2025 collapse).
- **The $16B-by-2030 operating-income claim (Q4 2024)** is the most reckless guidance artifact in the file — issued the same fiscal year the company swung to a −$713M loss. No director should weight it.

**Sandbagging pattern?** None in 2024 (they over-promised). A *deliberate* conservative skew appears only from Q4 2025 onward — "model toward the low end of the range," "counsel prudence in raising estimates prematurely" (Q1 2026). This is credibility-rebuilding behavior: having been burned for optimism, management now sets a low bar it can clear. That is rational, but it means **the 2026 guide is more believable precisely because management's track record forced them to lowball it.** The 57% beat rate and the catastrophic 2025 miss anchor reliability at **Low**, upgradeable to Medium only if 2026 actually lands in (or above) the $1.2–1.4B range.

---

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

Analysts repeatedly probed the exact fault lines that later became the bad news. Management's deflections are instructive in hindsight.

- **Bottlenecks / site capacity (Q2 2024, Gil Blum of Needham).** Ingram dismissed it: "I'm going to frustrate you by answering this question again... we don't have bottlenecks. We have a launch curve." Three quarters later (Q1 2025), capacity *was* the headline problem: "60% of our current revenue comes from top sites... fully booked out to 12 months." **The deflected question became the miss.**
- **Early Q4 trends (Q3 2024, Morgan Stanley's Rohit).** "We're not going to do that right now" — refused intra-quarter color while reiterating the $3B. The refusal preceded the collapse.
- **Payer coverage / denials (Q4 2024 H.C. Wainwright; Q1 2025 Barclays channel checks).** Management insisted "no kid... permanently denied therapy" and "ELEVIDYS, our current success rate stands at 100%." Analysts' channel checks ("some payers deciding not to cover ELEVIDYS") were brushed aside as PBM-vs-payer confusion. Access was reframed as a *timing* issue, "not about ultimate access" — a recurring deflection that masked the revenue-timing reality.
- **Liver safety / ALF cases (Q2 2025, Leerink's Will Soghikian).** Pressed on "how many patients have had ALF cases" and hospitalization trends, Ingram could not (or would not) supply the number: "I don't have that... if you're dehydrated, you get hospitalized." On a gene therapy with two deaths and a fresh black box, the inability to quantify the safety denominator is a genuine red flag analysts surfaced.
- **ESSENCE confirmatory risk (Q3 2024, Evercore's Gavin Clark-Gartner).** Asked bluntly about "requirements to actually pull these drugs off the market," management retreated to "the totality of evidence... not a yes or no based on one single trial." ## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Classification: PIVOTING (forced) — a deteriorated commercial core being defended by a strong balance sheet while the equity thesis migrates onto an unapproved pipeline.**

This is not a clean "deteriorating" story (the balance sheet and PMO base are genuinely solid, insiders are buying hard, and the ELEVIDYS *clinical* data is strengthening), nor is it "stable" (revenue is set to fall a further ~45% in 2026, the flagship lost 70%+ of its peak run-rate, a growth franchise was killed, and the confirmatory trial missed). It is a company that **over-promised spectacularly in 2024, was broken commercially in 2025 by safety events and execution, and is now executing a credible but unproven survival-and-reset.** Management's credibility on *narrative and clinical conviction* is high; its credibility on *delivering the numbers it forecasts* is low and was badly damaged.

**The single most important thing the director must weigh before sizing a position:** **Is the ELEVIDYS revenue collapse a *timing/information* problem (recoverable) or a permanent re-rating of a gene therapy whose risk-benefit the market and physicians have repriced after two deaths and a black box?** Everything turns on this. If management's "information deficit → re-education → return to growth" thesis is right, then $16.8 against net cash of ~$748M, a stable ~$900M/yr PMO base, and free pipeline optionality is a deep-value setup that insiders are correctly buying at ~7:1. If instead the hesitation is *rational physician response to a changed safety profile* — not a fixable information gap — then the 2026 guide is a *ceiling*, not a floor, the siRNA pipeline is the only real value, and the equity is an early-stage biotech wearing a commercial-company valuation. The director should **size to the cash floor and PMO annuity, treat ELEVIDYS recovery and siRNA as call options, and demand two pieces of hard evidence before adding: (1) a genuine, *quantified* ELEVIDYS start-form/revenue inflection in H2 2026, and (2) the ENDEAVOR Cohort 8 sirolimus readout (expected end-2026) reopening the non-ambulatory label.** Until those land, the burden of proof sits squarely with a management team that has already missed its biggest promise once.
